subject: Onboarding grant split & promotional expiry override for BrightLoop cohort
messages:
From: Jared Lopez <jared@brightloop.co>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Introductory grant for cohort — can we split it across startups?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — BrightLoop is excited about Redwood for cohort sandboxes. A quick question on the onboarding grant you mentioned: our accelerator usually gives a single stipend to the program, but we need to distribute it across 3 startups (separate workspaces). Is there a way to split the onboarding grant so each startup gets a portion and have a single invoice/sponsor flow on our side?

Other constraints:
- The sponsor (Foundry Fund) needs a 12-month expiry on the funds due to accounting.
- We might want the ability to convert leftover funds to a committed discount if a startup upgrades to Dedicated within 90 days.

Can you outline the options and any paperwork you need from us? We’re aiming to finalize terms before Nov 20 so teams can onboard before demo day.

Best,
Jared Lopez
Head of Programs | BrightLoop Labs
jared@brightloop.co

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lopez <jared@brightloop.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Introductory grant for cohort — can we split it across startups?

Hi Jared — great to hear, and love the timeline. Short answer: yes, we have a few paths we can take depending on how the sponsor wants funds managed. I’m outlining three practical options below and attaching the templates you’ll need.

Options:
1) Grant-splitting (fastest) — we issue the onboarding grant at program level and split it across N workspace IDs. Sponsor signs a single sponsor agreement; we map allocations to each workspace and set per-workspace expiries. This is what teams use most for cohorts.
2) Escrow-style sponsor invoice — sponsor pays Redwood and we hold the amount on our books with a 12-month expiry. We can apply funds to multiple workspaces on request. This requires a sponsor invoice/PO.
3) Convertible reserve — leftover stipend can be converted to a Dedicated discount/commit if a startup upgrades within an agreed window. This requires a short contract addendum (SOW addendum).

Tradeoffs: split grants are fast but we enforce per-workspace expiry by default. Escrow with sponsor invoicing lets us extend expiry to 12 months for accounting, but we need procurement details. The convertible reserve needs legal sign-off (simple addendum).

Attachments included:
- grant-split-template.pdf (fillable)
- sow-dedicated-addendum.docx (draft)
- pricing-matrix-202611.pdf (reference rates)

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the sponsor name and whether they prefer a single sponsor invoice (escrow) or program-level grant-split.
- If sponsor invoice: Ben (cc’d) will run the PO/invoice path and advise on net terms and minimums.
- If grant-split: fill the template and I’ll provision the workspace allocations within 48 hours of receipt.

I’m looping Ben for invoicing and Irene to flag any legal constraints on the convertible path. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Mid-Market — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Introductory grant for cohort — can we split it across startups?

Thanks Tessa — quick note from finance/partnerships side.

If Foundry Fund will sign a single sponsor PO, we can put the funds on our balance sheet and extend the expiry to 12 months. We typically require a minimum monthly consumption threshold to enable extended expiry and avoid long-tail accounting — for this cohort I recommend a 3-month ramp commitment of $3k/month aggregated across startups (flexible by write-up). If they prefer pure grant-splitting with no PO, expiry defaults to 90 days per workspace.

On the convertible reserve: we can allow unused funds to be applied as a one-time committed discount if the startup signs Dedicated within 90 days of the stipend being applied. Legal needs to add a short addendum to any acceptance form (Irene, see attached draft).

Operational asks for sponsor invoice route:
- Sponsor name exactly as it should appear on PO and remit-to
- Billing contact, PO number (if available), and any special invoice notes
- Preferred net terms (Net30/Net45)

I’ve created the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5421 — and I can generate the invoice once we have PO details. For DocuSign we can push the addendum here: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABCD1234

Jared — if you can confirm sponsor preference (PO vs grant-split) and whether the sponsor can agree to the nominal $3k/month ramp, we’ll pick the path and I’ll kick off invoice generation.

— Ben
